blurb: A package's units are resolved against the packages it depends on, so the package graph needs an order: no package may depend, directly or through others, on itself or on the project. A cycle usually means two packages each want something of the other. Move what both need into a third package that each of them depends on, or merge the two.
example:
# packages/money/bynk.toml
[dependencies]
tax = { package = "acme/tax", path = "../tax" }

# packages/tax/bynk.toml
[dependencies]
money = { package = "acme/money", path = "../money" }   // ✗ `acme/money` depends on `acme/tax`

core = { package = "acme/core", path = "../core" }      // ✓ what both need, in a package of its own
summary: The package graph has a cycle: a dependency depends, directly or not, on itself or on the project.
